Jamie (eng-runtime): quick q — trying to repro a KV-cache eviction spike in a short smoke run. what's the minimal nsys profile flags you all use to get a clean kernel timeline (and NVTX markers) without 5GB trace files?
Sophia: for quick repros i do bracketed capture + sampling and nvtx. keeps file small and shows kernel handoffs.
Jamie (eng-runtime): can you paste the exact cmd you use? i tried `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=run` for 30s and got a 1.2GB file with a lot of warmup noise.
Matt: i usually do a warmup window outside capture, then bracket: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --duration=12 --capture-range=process:<PID>` and put a small sleep before the interesting load. that reduces sampling overhead and still yields kernel timelines.
Ravi: fwiw `--sample=none` is good if you rely on cuda timelines + nvtx. sampling is helpful for CPU stacks but bloats file. also add `--capture-range=nvtx:marker1:marker2` if you can emit markers from runtime.
Jamie (eng-runtime): good call — we already have NVTX push/pop around batch boundaries, didn't think to bracket on markers.
Sophia: alternative: short sampled run if you need CPU call stacks: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --sample-interval=1000 --duration=15` — sample-interval trades fidelity for size.
Matt: also watch `--osrt` on older drivers, it can generate lots of OSRT events; sometimes filter it out if you only care about kernels: `--trace=cuda,nvtx` will be much leaner.
Ravi: if you're debugging kernel selection differences, capture two runs back-to-back with identical inputs and compare timelines in Nsight: save as `run_a.qdrep`/`run_b.qdrep` then open both and do a kernel timeline diff. highlights kernel switching.
Jamie (eng-runtime): how do you handle KV cache warmup? the first few requests evict and throw off the timeline.
Sophia: warm the KV cache before capture with a deterministic prefix set (same batch sizes). simplest: run a scripted warmup that touches keys, then `sleep 0.5` and start the bracketed capture.
Matt: if warmup is expensive, capture a narrow window around the eviction moment: emit NVTX marker just before you trigger the pathological request and end capture right after. reduces noise and file size.
Ravi: for regressions, add a tiny CSV log of per-request meta (seq len, batch size, chosen kernel name) alongside the trace. makes it trivial to map timeline spikes -> request attributes.
Jamie (eng-runtime): great — i'll try bracketed nvtx capture + `--sample=none` and warmup script. one last Q: recommended duration for a single eviction spike? 8-12s?
Sophia: 8s is usually enough if you bracket on NVTX and exclude warmup. 12s if you want a couple of async callbacks in the tail.
Matt: also compress qdrep when archiving with `nsys stats`? i just keep the qdrep and a small extracted CSV of kernels as the canonical artifact.
perf-bot: reminder — large traces (>1GB) should be uploaded to our perf-s3 bucket and referenced in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark: 
Jamie (eng-runtime): thanks everyone — will post results and the smaller qdrep link once i have it. :thumbsup:
